text: Each role comes with a sensible set of permissions. When your practice needs something different, the role editor changes it for that role.
The one thing to remember: a change to a role applies to everyone with that role. And Not enforced yet means that switch does nothing today.
Open the role you want to change: Client Liaison.
Every change here applies to everyone with this role.
Each permission says Yes, No, or Their own only. Default is what Scout ships with. Client liaisons don't create bank deposits by default.
Only show changes lists what this practice has changed.
Some permissions say Not enforced yet. Scout doesn't check them yet, so changing them does nothing. Don't rely on them.
Hover the tag for the reason.
To make a change, pick the new setting, then Save. Reset puts one back to the default, and Discard throws away unsaved changes.
We'll leave this one as it is.
The most common mistakes: changing a role to fix one person, which changes it for everyone, and switching off a permission marked Not enforced yet, and thinking it's blocked.
Remember: a role change applies to everyone with that role.
